Wet macular degeneration occurs in about 1 in 10 people and occurs when abnormal blood vessels, which are very fragile, grow under the retina.  Fluid then leaks from the vessels causing damage to the retina resulting in loss of central vision.  So the distinguishing factor between wet and dry macular degeneration is the blood vessels.

Wet macular degeneration should be treated by a retina specialist.  You can find an ophthalmologist or optometrist who is a retina specialist on the American Society of Retina Specialists website or ask your local eye doctor for a recommendation on a specialist in your area.
